summary:
Implemented the terminal window title setting in the rich repository, by reading and editing files only. Nothing was run or committed.

Changes:
- rich/segment.py: added SET_WINDOW_TITLE = 16 as the last ControlType member, and Tuple[ControlType, str] to the ControlCode union.
- rich/control.py: added a formatter entry producing ESC ] 0 ; title BEL, and a Control.title(title) classmethod that passes (ControlType.SET_WINDOW_TITLE, title) as one argument, with a docstring.
- rich/console.py: added Console.set_window_title(title) -> bool after show_cursor. It checks only is_terminal, writes the control and returns True, or returns False with nothing written. Google-style docstring with the required caveats.
- rich/_windows_renderer.py: added one elif branch to the legacy dispatch chain that calls term.set_title(title) on the second item of the code. The Win32 wrapper is unchanged.
- CHANGELOG.md: created an Added section under Unreleased, above Fixed, with one bullet linking pull request 2200.
- Tests: Control.title segment and control-list test in tests/test_control.py; set_window_title console test in tests/test_console.py (skipped on win32); mocked set_title renderer test in tests/test_windows_renderer.py.

Choices: the console test's legacy-Windows skip uses sys.platform == "win32". Title text is passed through unescaped, per the spec, so a title containing BEL or ESC would end the sequence early.

Verification: none. Tests and mypy were not run, per instructions, so pass/fail status is unknown.
